title: Prevention of Care Dependency through Prevention Nursing
summary:
This study investigates whether the new form of care, "Prevention Nursing," can preserve independence in older adults with mild cognitive impairment. Participants are people aged 65 and above who applied for recognition of a care level but did not receive a recommendation from the  the medical service of the health insurance fund (Medizinischer Dienst). The study is divided on a randomized basis: one group receives "Prevention Nursing," while the other group continues to receive care as usual. The "Prevention Nursing" group receives individualized support from a specially trained professional, known as the Prevention Nurse. The goal is to improve mobility, cognition, social participation, the care situation, and nutrition according to individual needs. This is carried out in collaboration with the participant's general practitioner and family members. 

All participants are assessed at three time points: at the start of the study, after eight months, and after 15 months. Established tests and questionnaires are used, including a memory test and a test to assess nutritional status. In addition, participants' medications are reviewed for potential risks, and it is examined whether loneliness is a relevant issue for participants.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Applied for a formal recognition of a care level (Pflegegrad), but did not receive a recommendation from the  the medical service of the health insurance fund (Medizinischer Dienst)
- MoCA score > 18 and < 26 (indicating mild cognitive impairment)
- Member of statutory health insurance
- Informed consent to study participation and data collection (written consent)
- Sufficient language comprehension to understand the study information and follow study procedures
- Community-dwelling
Exclusion criteria:
- Repeat application for a formal recognition of a care level (e.g., appeal or renewed application following a prior rejection) at the time of recruitment, as well as application for upgrading to a higher care level or for inpatient long-term care
- Any circumstances that preclude participation (e.g., lack of capacity to consent without legal representation)
